newsitem.title: BELGIUM: All set for tv directive conciliation talks.
newsitem.headline: All set for tv directive conciliation talks.

text.p: The Council of Ministers and European Parliament are set to launch the conciliation procedure on revisions to the draft television without frontiers directive, EU officials said on Monday.
The date for the start of the talks -- pencilled in as March 20 -- is expected to be confirmed in Strasbourg this week.

The start of the talks, which will have up to six weeks to succeed, was made possible after the Committee of Permanent Representatives settled the Council's own position for the talks last week, sweeping away a reservation from Spain and France over the retroactive nature of an arrangement for exclusive sports rights.
"There is no Spanish problem any more," one official said.

In its second reading on plans to revise the television without frontiers directive 89/552/EEC the parliament demanded an article ensuring access for non-paying viewers when pay television channels snap up exclusive rights to major sporting events like the soccer World Cup and Olympic Games.

The Council has broadly accepted a Commission proposal that member states be able to require mutual recognition by pay television operators from other member states of national lists of major sporting events which should be shown in clear.
Although Germany maintains reservations to the plan, this will not prevent the Council taking its position to the negotiating table with the parliament, officials said.
While the Council has taken on board one of the parliament's two major amendments, the second is set to fall by the wayside in the trade off.
The parliament in November demanded that all television sets be fitted with anti-violence chips to allow parents to screen their children from violent programmes.
The Commission and Council, citing lack of technical feasibility, are unwilling to take on the idea and the parliament is showing no sign of pushing it.
